free_tier.stated: 'Upload your personal files to a secure cloud storage system ... You get 1 TB of space'.
free_tier.notes: The 1 TB claim is on the landing page and on its premium subdomain, which serve the same text. The vendor terms state 'We provide Only premium subscription services.' and the landing text does not call the 1 TB free, so whether a free account keeps that space is unverified.

per_object_cap.stated: 3 GB maximum size of an uploaded file (for a Premium user), per the vendor terms.

retention.stated: not stated on the pages read; the only related statement is that 'a premium user can restrict' access to their own files

egress.terms: Premium users are limited to 55GB of download per day (24 hours), changeable at the administration's discretion (vendor terms). The vendor publishes no free download volume; free_allowance holds the third-party figure.
egress.price_per_tb: USD 19.00 per 30 days for ~1,5 TB; USD 45.00 per 90 days for ~5 TB; USD 75.00 per 180 days for ~10 TB (vendor premium page)

interface_detail: Web upload and file manager on a subdomain (premium.isra.cloud). No API was found; the vendor publishes no endpoint.
tooling: Browser only as read. Both Leechall and PrimeLeech carry an isra.cloud generator, so a leecher is the only scripted pull found.
chaining: The 1 TB storage figure is the headline, but the vendor publishes no free download volume. The vendor sells premium plans on its own premium page (USD 19.00 for 30 days, USD 45.00 for 90 days, USD 75.00 for 180 days) and resellers list the same durations in EUR.

limits.value: 1 TB of storage on the free account

limits_note: The 1 TB is storage, not transfer. The only free-download figure is third-party, so if it holds the ratio between the two makes the free side unusable as a transfer path; the premium side is stated in the vendor terms.
binding_note: Premium plans are sold by bandwidth (about 1,5 TB for 30 days, about 5 TB for 90 days, about 10 TB for 180 days); the vendor publishes no free download volume.

identity_cost.detail: Sign-up page /register.html ('User Registration') with a captcha code; the form fields did not render in the capture. The premium page says 'To purchase a premium access you need to be a registered, verified and authorized user.' Premium is sold on the vendor premium page and through resellers labelled 'Official Reseller'.

reliability_note: The terms state the per-day allowance can be changed at the administration's discretion, and that a premium user's files may not be downloadable by another account even with premium.
confidence_note: The 1 TB storage sentence is the vendor's own; its terms say 'We provide Only premium subscription services.', so whether a free account keeps that space is unverified. The premium plans, the 3 GB upload cap and the premium daily figure are vendor pages; the free daily transfer cap is a third-party statement.
